crates.name: keyring
crates.purpose: Linux Secret Service behaviour spike (P00-T07); default feature v1 selects zbus-secret-service-keyring-store with crypto-rust on Linux; T03 primary
notes: P00 closure clarification (2026-10-24): frozen as a spike dependency inventory entry; this is not permission to build or adopt it in P01+ (separate approved dependency request required).

P00 closure clarification (2026-10-24): the K-A advisory exception is HISTORICAL/INACTIVE: valid only for the completed, authorised P00-T07 experiment and its original lockfile (eeca61f5…) and scope; NOT applicable to the current frozen lockfile (a81eec56…). No additional keyring build or production adoption is authorised; any future build or adoption needs a new explicit owner decision and advisory re-screen (FR-24). The advisories are not suppressed globally.

Accepted for the tested isolated setup only (private bus and service; K01a, K01b, K02, K03, K04, K04b, K05, K06). NOT accepted: direct synchronous keyring calls in the main application, persistent credential storage as a pilot or product feature, native cancellation of blocked operations, real desktop-prompter behaviour, other Secret Service implementations or normal login sessions, complete leakage or dependency-safety assurance.

Suitability finding: an unresponsive bus blocks the library indefinitely (K06) and store initialisation is cached per process; FR-18 to FR-24 apply to any future OS-store implementation (P03). Session-only mode remains required.

The advisory exceptions are the spike-only K-A exception for the unmaintained notices on zvariant 5.15.1, zbus_names 4.3.5 and zvariant_derive 5.15.1 reached through keyring -> zbus-secret-service-keyring-store -> zbus 5.19.0 (informational unmaintained, consolidated into zbus 6.0.0; no secret-service release uses zbus 6 at the lookup). Scope: this spike only, exact versions/checksums/paths of the locked graph; not an advisory-ignore configuration; does not extend to other advisories, versions, graphs, P01+ workspaces or any production or release build.

The exception text binds to Cargo.lock SHA-256 eeca61f5f8b505efd2985bebb0466f5d7f6c98ca8fd7ea8624287b3877bf099c (after T07 stage A). The current lockfile hash differs because T08 stage A added packages by lock-preserving resolution (no existing package version changed, evidence/P00/P00-T08/record.md). The exception text says any re-resolution voids it; whether it still applies to the current lockfile is NOT decided in any record and is an owner/Opus question.
Mandatory review points: re-screen the whole backend path and re-decide the exception before P03 adoption and again before any release (FR-24).
The cli feature (dbus-secret-service-keyring-store with vendored libdbus) is not enabled and must not be.

Build-time code: 10 build scripts and 9 proc-macro crates in the T07 host graph plus proc-macro-crate spawning `cargo locate-project` at compile time; accepted for this locked spike build only; no filesystem sandbox.

build_rules: Build and test each spike per package (-p <package>), never --workspace and never several spike packages in one Cargo invocation (resolver 2 feature unification; T06+T07 and T06+T08 and T07+T08 combined builds add features to shared crates and would need a targeted retest) (evidence/P00/P00-T07/record.md, evidence/P00/P00-T08/record.md, handover.md).
Pin direct dependencies with exact `=` versions exactly as recorded; no feature beyond the recorded set without owner approval; dependency upgrades need approval and re-verification (FR-14).

Invoke the toolchain binaries directly (~/.rustup/toolchains/stable-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/bin/{cargo,rustc}), not through a rustup proxy, so no toolchain update can occur; record `rustc -vV` (evidence/P00/P00-T05-D3-1/record.md).

Run every Cargo command under `env -i` with only PATH, HOME, CARGO_HOME, CARGO_TARGET_DIR, RUSTC (and CARGO_TERM_COLOR=never); CARGO_HOME and CARGO_TARGET_DIR isolated under ~/.local/share/pwt-dev-tools/ (cache and output separation only, not a sandbox); no API keys, tokens or unrelated variables; global ~/.cargo not used (evidence/P00/P00-T05-D3-1/record.md).
Before Cargo runs, confirm no .cargo/config or .cargo/config.toml exists in any ancestor of spikes/rust/ (Cargo reads those regardless of CARGO_HOME).

Resolution after the first member uses lock-preserving `cargo update --workspace` (dry-run first), not `cargo generate-lockfile`, which re-resolves every package; check that no existing package version changed and that sources are crates.io and local only (evidence/P00/P00-T07/record.md, evidence/P00/P00-T08/record.md). Any re-resolution voids the T07 advisory exception.

Fetch with `cargo fetch --locked --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`, independently verify each .crate SHA-256 against Cargo.lock, and compare Cargo.lock and manifest hashes before and after every step.

Build offline and locked inside a network namespace: `unshare -rn env -i ... cargo build --frozen [--offline] -p <package>`; network absence is enforced by the namespace, not by --offline. There is no filesystem sandbox: build scripts and proc-macros run with the user's file permissions, and grep-based pattern review is not an audit.

Run spike binaries only through the recorded namespace commands (harnesses refuse to run unless PID 1 of a user+net+PID namespace; verified environment check first; outer timeout -s KILL watchdog) and never outside them.

Screen the locked graph against RustSec advisories before build (published advisories only; absence is not evidence of safety); cargo-audit is deferred to P01. Stop and report on any applicable unresolved advisory; the only exception is the T07 K-A spike-only exception.
Use bash arrays for Cargo option lists in wrapper scripts (the zsh word-splitting exit-127 trap recurred in T06, T07 and T08).
The spike workspace is development-only and not part of the product build; the freeze does not approve any dependency for application use.
